minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved several septic, home and tree permits and continued three hearings to October 5.
minutes.summary: The commission held hearings on wetlands filings. It approved a septic replacement, a Townsend Harbor Road home and two Holman Street homes. It continued three other hearings to October 5 for missing plans or a missing DEP file number. It also accepted an encroachment fix at 100 Woodland Drive, approved a pollinator-habitat fencing purchase, and appointed a member to the stormwater committee.

budget_items.topic: DEP habitat study and filing fees for shoreline wall
budget_items.what_was_said: An applicant's engineer said a shoreline stone wall would require a costly habitat study and higher DEP filing fees, so the applicant dropped it.
Three quotes were in for window replacement at the Hollis Road residence, with one more day open. Quotes for kitchen cabinets and countertops were also starting to arrive.

decisions.decision: Election of officers was put off to a future meeting because not all members were present.
The 75 West Street enforcement order was taken off the agenda. The homeowners will work directly with the conservation agent on revegetation and removal of erosion controls.
The commission only acknowledged the Lake Shirley floating mat removal notice, since it was already covered by an approved order of conditions.
The commission asked the 408 Electric Ave applicant to update the plan to show the driveway, gravel and other existing features before it would act.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a septic replacement at 290 New West Townsend Road with standard conditions, by unanimous roll call.
It approved the 451 Townsend Harbor Road house filing, with one member recused, and approved homes on Lots 3 and 4 Holman Street unanimously.
Three hearings, at 408 Electric Ave, 509 Townsend Harbor Road and 127 Chase Road, were continued to October 5 for missing plan details or a DEP file number.
The commission accepted the encroachment fix at 100 Woodland Drive and approved a purchase order for pollinator-habitat fencing to protect new trees from deer.
It appointed Richard Tremblay to the stormwater committee, and put off the election of officers because not all members were present.

why_it_matters: Wetlands approvals set the conditions for septic systems and new homes near protected resources, and an applicant whose plan is incomplete waits a full meeting cycle for a decision.
The fencing purchase is a small town expense, chosen from three quotes, that shows how the commission spends on habitat work.
watch_next: The October 5 meeting, when the 408 Electric Ave, 509 Townsend Harbor Road and 127 Chase Road hearings resume.
The future meeting where the commission is to hold its election of officers.
